quality_notes.detail: The tree is parsed from LankaLaw, a private republisher. A Government Printer edition of this Act exists, has a text layer, and was used to check the parse -- but the text below is still LankaLaw's transcription, and the two differ in wording throughout.

Section 10's marginal note, "Preparation of Cadastral plans and maps.", was printed inside the body of subsection (1). It is corrected into the heading and left in raw_text and text, where it still interrupts the sentence.

Sections 10 (2), 25 (1) and 25 (2) each open a lettered pair and the source marks up only the (b) limb, so (a) is carried inside the subsection's own text rather than as a paragraph node. Not synthesised: inventing the container would change the tree on inference alone. Both editions print (a) and (b).

Section 66 defines 15 terms in the Government Printer edition. This tree types 11. "Cadastral survey" is untyped because the parsed edition drops its opening quotation mark, and "Department" because a stray full stop is printed before its opening quote; both are held as closing_text nodes beside the definitions and carry their full wording. "Minister" is absent from the parsed edition, "registered licensed surveyor" is run on inside another entry, and one entry is blank.

Section 39 requires the qualifications specified in the Schedule, and the parsed page carries no Schedule. The body under `schedules` was read off the Government Printer edition and is marked as such; it is not part of the parse.

No amending Act is recorded for this Act in this corpus and the parsed page carries no amendment chain in its header. That is the absence of a finding, not a finding of no amendments: nothing here has checked the Gazette.

quality_notes.issue: Subsections printed out of order/mislabelled in the source itself, confirmed against the raw HTML line-by-line: s.2 prints (1),(2),(1A),(1B),(3) in that literal sequence (the 1982 insert was appended after (2) rather than spliced in after (1)); s.4's Board-membership list runs (i),(j),(k) then a list item printed as (1) where (l) is expected (an l/1 confusion), then resumes at (m),(n).

Section 26B's heading and text are embedded inside section 26A's own content block rather than under their own tagged section anchor, so the shared parser reads them as part of 26A and no separate 26B section is emitted.

A nested lettered list restarts at (a)/(b) inside an outer paragraph also lettered (a)/(b) (e.g. s.28A(3): the outer '(a) Where any person has failed ... authorizing the Authority to-' introduces its own '(a) to discontinue...', '(b) to demolish...', '(c) to do such other acts...'). The splitter does not recognise a lone letter preceded by an ordinary word as a new list item -- by design, to avoid worse false positives such as splitting 'referred to in paragraph (a)' -- so the outer paragraph's own lettered limb stays folded into its text instead of becoming its own child.

s.19G(2) reads 'Sections 321, 322 (1), 322 (2), 324, 325, 326, 328 (c), 329 and 330 of the Code of Criminal Procedure Act, No. 15 of 1979' -- all nine are external to this Act. Only '321' was captured, and as an internal cross-reference (this Act has no section 321); 322-330 are dropped entirely. The external-reference regex does not handle a comma-separated run of section/subsection pairs this long before the enactment name.

schedules.heading: SCHEDULE
schedules.quality_notes: Recovered from the consolidated statute PDF (data/legal-sources/library/statutes/41-1978-urban-development-authority-act.pdf, pages 30-32), not the LankaLaw HTML, which never carries the Schedule's text. Includes the amendment by Act 36 of 2007 to item 4(e) that the prior OCR-sourced version was missing. The source itself skips item 15 and prints item 16 twice ('16. The redistribution...' followed immediately by '16. The demarcation...'); confirmed identical under both naive and layout-preserving (pdftotext -layout) extraction, so this is a defect in the consolidated PDF's own typesetting, not an extraction artifact, and is left as printed rather than renumbered.
schedules.text:
1. The manner in which the land and buildings in the development area shall be used.

2. The allotment, reservation or zoning of land for different purposes.

3. The provision for regulating the uses of land and buildings in different zones such as residential, commercial, industrial and imposition of conditions and restrictions in regard to the floor area ratio, density, location, and height, number of storey and size of building and structures, the size of plots, yards and open spaces, set backs from street, building lines and the use and maintenance of buildings, structures and appurtenant land.

4. The requirements for buildings in respect of -

(a) stability of different parts of buildings foundations and super-structure;

(b) area and height, levels of floors, standards of accommodation for rooms, location and standards for staircases and exits;

(c) lighting and ventilation;

(d) fire protection;

(e) drainage of site and roof including measures necessary for rainwater harvesting; [3,36 of 2007]

(f) specifications for materials of construction and code of practice;

(g) standards and materials for plumbing and waste disposal, electrical wiring and installation such as pumps and lifts;

(h) regulations regarding clear distances of buildings from electrical, telephone, telegraph and microwave and other lines.

(i) regulations in respect of unsafe buildings and prescribing standards of fitness for buildings and other matters incidental to the ensuring of stability, safety and amenity of buildings.

5. The control of architectural features, elevation and frontage of buildings and regulations for attaining urban design objectives.

6. The provision for preserving and promoting landscaping including preservation and planting of woodlands, trees and preservation of views and prospects, places of historical, architectural interest and scenic beauty.

7. The control of pollution, environmental quality and advertisement.

8. The provision for car parking facilities, parking, loading and service bays for all types of vehicles.

9. The provisions for matters concerning and incidental to- (a) traffic and transport facilities including special facilities for pedestrians and cyclists; (b) water supply, sewerage and drainage and waste disposal facilities; (c) power supply; (d) telecommunication.

10. The provision for laying out of land for building purposes including minimum standards for access ways and roads, reservation of parks, play grounds and open spaces for other amenities and the imposition of conditions requiring the amount of land to construct or improve roads, and provide amenities or to contribute to the cost of such construction or improvement.

11. Provisions for reclamation of land.

12. The laying out and relaying out of land either vacant or already built upon, as building sites.

13. The construction, diversion, extension, alteration, improvement or closure of lanes, streets, roads and communications.

14. The construction, alteration, removal or demolition of buildings, bridges and other structures.

16. The redistribution of boundaries and the reconstitution of plots belonging to owners of property.

16. The demarcation of areas for special treatment and their detailed planning, development and redevelopment.

17. The stages by which the development plan shall be carried out.

18. The levy of fees and service charges in respect of different categories of developments.

SRC042.note: Tree built from pre-2012 LankaLaw HTML edition (1981 revised-edition snapshot). Coverage check vs 2024 consolidated PDF revealed Section 5 and related sections show pre-amendment wording from 1939, superseded by amendments Act 21 of 2017, Act 21 of 2012, Act 24 of 1977, and others.

quality_notes.issue: A '(i)' that opens a single-item nested list stays folded into its parent's own text instead of becoming its own child, while a later '(ii)' in the same list correctly splits out as a sibling node -- so the tree shows an orphaned '(ii)' with no '(i)'. Two distinct shapes cause this: s.36(e) prints '(e) (i) to sell, exchange...', two enumerator markers directly adjacent with no lead-in prose; s.74 and s.78 have '...aggregate of (i) the estimated cost...', a marker straight after an ordinary word. A general fix for the first shape (treating a closing paren as a list-introducing character before the next marker) was tried and reverted: it also fires on citation chains like 'subsection (1) or (4) (a) or (b) or (c)', which are one continuous cross-reference, not a new list, and it corrupted that pattern across 25 other statutes in a full-corpus rebuild. The second shape is the same word-boundary ambiguity already documented for SRC039 (s.74/s.78's '(i)' looks identical to a genuine reference like 'referred to in paragraph (a)'), so it is not split either, by the same design choice.
